boundedSanskritTokens.function: Mercury epithet in the relationship listing
Mercury form retained as a distinct source token

mandatoryCells.grammaticalOrientationExplanation: The Mars-held relationship list identifies Mercury as an enemy target. The program therefore records MARS -> MERCURY, not the inverse.
The Mercury-held enemy statement separately names Mars as its target. It is not a restatement of the Mars-held clause, so the program records MERCURY -> MARS independently.
The same Mercury-held enemy statement separately names Moon. The program records MERCURY -> MOON without deriving it from Moon's row.
The Moon-held friend listing identifies Mercury as a friend target. The program records MOON -> MERCURY, independently of Mercury's enemy relation to Moon.

neutralityRule.explanation: Verse 4.29 supplies the residual neutral rule after the named friend and enemy lists. It is not inferred from Trailokya, a modern table, or symmetry.

paginationCorrections.reason: The Sanskrit roots physically end at the bottom of printed p.57/PDF image 61; p.58/PDF image 62 contains the separate English rendering.
The Saravali root locator is corrected without changing the retained Brihat Jataka or Trailokya locators.
